title: Coverage limits and next evidence for the Eucharistic book-stage chronology
scope: Coverage crosswalk of the canonical candidate inventories and stage dossiers at the input hashes below. This audit reconciles their declared evidence, witnesses and gaps; it creates no stages, transitions, local reception claims or text-completion claims.

count_semantics.warning: These count different objects. The 23 Eastern rows are research slots, not a resolved current official taxonomy; 151 Western routes include composite and overlapping discovery buckets; 233 presentation groups are display categories. Candidates and catalogue clusters are not distinct recensions, complete books or locally received versions.
count_semantics.source_route_scope: The 708 source routes preserve prior audit entries and add newly admitted source IDs, reconciled to URLs in the 409 Eastern and 1314 Western source records; this is not a count of source books or of all inventory source records.

findings: Retain every existing coverage row, including index-only and unresearched local uses, alongside selected new dossiers.
A missing unique Church edition is not itself a gap: one source book may serve several communities. Missing exact book identity and local reception evidence are real gaps.

Slovak reception of the shared Lviv 1905 book and later source-language exemplars is source-described. Official translation approvals are now identified; exact source copies and dated local implementation remain separate questions.

Albanian and Macedonian exact received source-language books remain unidentified. A Macedonian translation approval is recorded without establishing its exemplar. Bulgarian Vulgata audience evidence still does not establish actual adoption.
Roman Greek, Ruthenian and Vulgata, Coptic and Ge’ez, and the separate East/West Syriac Catholic lines must not become single family-wide evolutionary chains.
Publication, approval, effective implementation and modern editorial publication dates are separate. Candidate witness bounds below are not stage-validity intervals.
A component, complementary volume or appended calendar does not represent an entire successive Eucharistic book.
No assigned new dossier covers the full early sacramentary corpus or all Sarum/York/Hereford/continental diocesan and monastic trajectories.

Selected local-use, canonical-order and Slavonic Roman stages now resolve to their own dossiers. Composite discovery rows retain unmapped communities and incomplete periods; no dossier supplies whole-book text completeness.
Complete native constituents count as partial book coverage. Recorded book states, optional rules and complementary volumes do not create a complete missal or authorize text inheritance.

The 2026-10-20 regional dossier adds seven bounded book states (two provisional) and one provisional source-described Polish printing transition; no whole-book text completion or unexamined first-use date follows.
A second source-bounded review adds Bursfelde, Évora, Nidaros, Turku, Zagreb, Prague, Blaj and German diocesan book states; it adds no unverified revision transition or complete text.

A further bounded review records 83 exact book states across Eastern, early Western, French, Italian, northwest and central European, and order-specific routes. These are witness states, not continuous histories; no new transition or whole-book text completion is inferred.

The Ukrainian Church’s 2024 promulgated Ukrainian service text is retained as a received operative language candidate; observed first celebration and the complete printed volume remain to be inspected.

Seven Central European dated stages now point to exact book candidates instead of broad discovery clusters; the Hospitaller 1553 stage points to the identified BnF B-320 copy, leaving other Lyon copies unmerged.
Residual Western and order review adds only exact source-bounded book states; composite discovery rows and deferred translations remain research gaps, not invented rites or revisions.

The next accepted phase adds 30 exact inventory witnesses, 79 source rows, five bounded French repertoire routes and 15 bounded states with one source-described Hungarian witness-succession. The 678-row Amiet crosswalk is preserved without converting unmatched IDs or 98 origin labels into rites or recensions. Local reception, original source books/approval instruments, competing dates and whole-book text gaps remain explicit. Two complete native Cistercian offertory constituents remain partial whole books. Nine earlier witness-date snapshots now follow canonical structured chronology, including deliberate nulls.

Batch 3 adds seven bounded Western publication attestations and a fourth associated Ravenna fragment while retaining Huesca original-book acquisition and local-reception gaps. The new Cistercian post-Canon/Pater constituents supply no whole-book completion or ancestry; wider 1657 source damage is named explicitly.

sources.title: Michal Glevaňák, Prešovská eparchiálna synoda, jej liturgické ustanovenia a ich implikácia do liturgického života, Theologos 1/2006, 106–126
sources.inspection: Read PDF text layer, printed pp.117–121; especially p.119 and notes 57–58. Page-image requests failed; original archival documents and book were not inspected.
sources.limitations: Original research reproducing and discussing archival evidence. Source-described reception, not independently collated act or source book.

sources.title: Jan Dominik Bogataj, O novem slovenskem prevodu Božje liturgije, Edinost in dialog 77/2 (2022), 247–264
sources.inspection: Read PDF text layer pp.249–250, 259–261 and 263, including source-book identification and approval-letter references.
sources.limitations: Firsthand translator account. Original approval letters and exact 1942 copy not inspected; scope is Križevci and its Slovenian translation.

sources.title: Ilya V. Semenenko-Basin and Stefano Caprio, Русские литургические памяти в славянском византо-католическом месяцеслове (Recensio Vulgata) середины XX в., Slověne 10/1 (2021), 368–391
sources.inspection: Read PDF text layer pp.369, 375–376, 382–384 and 389. Authors report direct examination of 1950 and 1953 books.
sources.limitations: Audience and scholarly comparison are usable at source-described level; no Bulgarian or Serbian copy or implementation act inspected.

sources.title: Bulgarian Catholic Apostolic Exarchate, Издания
sources.inspection: Read rendered publication paragraph naming ДОЙДОХМЕ, ЗА ДА МУ СЕ ПОКЛОНИМ — служебник, часослов, молитвеник, Burgas 2005, issued for Cologne World Youth Day.
sources.limitations: Publication listing only; no title leaf, contents, language, celebrant status or approval examined.

sources.title: Slovak Greek Catholic mission, Munich: Posvätenie liturgických kníh, 19 June 2022
sources.inspection: Read 19 June entry describing blessing of German, Slovak and Church Slavonic liturgikons, Apostolos, Gospels and Trebnik.
sources.limitations: Attests books and received language in one community, but no exact imprint or source edition.

sources.title: Metropolitan Cantor Institute, The Liturgikon
sources.inspection: Read Church Slavonic section and contents description: Lviv 1905, Roman 1942, and division from Horologion and other books.
sources.limitations: Institutional retrospective; exact source editions not independently inspected. Current English-book regulations not audited.

sources.title: L’Osservatore Romano, New edition of Missal in Ge’ez
sources.inspection: Read entire article describing 27 May 2025 presentation, joint Ethiopian/Eritrean commissions and hoped-for common use.
sources.limitations: No exact title/front matter or effective date inspected. Joint publication does not establish uniform implementation.

sources.title: Benedict XIV, Ex quo primum, 1 March 1756
sources.inspection: Read Italian rendered text, 1754 publication account and concluding conformity instruction with 1756 dateline.
sources.limitations: Broad Greek-rite direction; does not identify copies or actual reception in every present Church.

sources.title: Holy See Press Office, Synod for the Middle East presentation, Eastern Church historical sheet, 7 October 2010
sources.inspection: Read historical Church descriptions, especially Albanian, Italo-Albanian, Križevci and Macedonian entries.
sources.limitations: Historical institutional context only. Uses a pre-Eritrean census and is not a current census authority. No book identified.

sources.title: Bishop Stojanov pastoral letter on five years of the Strumica-Skopje eparchy
sources.inspection: Whole provider HTML acquired and complete pastoral-letter body read on 2026-10-20; HTML lines 864–881, especially 876. Source publication 4 December 2023, 08:27. Requests thanksgiving liturgies on 3 December 2023.
sources.limitations: Institutional history and a requested celebration only; does not name a celebrant edition, language, source exemplar, or establish actual celebration or operative reception of the 2009 approved wording.

sources.title: Usuarium: Missalia project reports
sources.inspection: Read the 11 December 2025 report and 20 February 2023 Iberian report, including links to Barcelona, Salamanca, Seville and Toledo records.
sources.limitations: The project's own account of coverage; its books, institutions and uses are not interchangeable counts. No independent full census performed.

sources.title: Usuarium 48: Missale Barcinonense
sources.inspection: Read bibliographic fields, fragment warning and contents index. Catalogue gives 1498, Didacus de Gumiel, Biblioteca de Catalunya Inc. 46-Fol.; surviving span begins at Holy Saturday and ends at 25 January.
sources.limitations: Catalogue metadata only. Original page images not inspected. Holding-platform link failed with cache miss.

sources.title: Usuarium 55: Missale Salmanticense
sources.inspection: Read bibliographic fields and contents index: 1533, Ioannes Junta, BU Salamanca BG/18686; title page at catalogue image 5, decree/calendar at 7 and colophon at 609. Also read the beginning of the linked conspectus, without verifying against images.
sources.limitations: Original page images and decree not inspected. Holding-platform handle failed with cache miss. No revision established.

sources.title: Usuarium 57: Missale Hispalense
sources.inspection: Read bibliographic fields and contents index: 1565, Ioannes Gutiérrez, BU Sevilla A Res. 10/1/06; title at catalogue image 14, preface/decree at 16, colophon at 682 (328v).
sources.limitations: Original images uninspected; linked Spanish heritage record returned HTTP 429. The catalogue's decree label is not an independent authentication of a normative act.

sources.title: Usuarium 60: Missale Toletanum
sources.inspection: Read bibliographic fields, explicit Roman-use classification and contents index: 1551, Bartholomaeus Fraenus, BM Lyon SJ L 013/14. Catalogue locates title/decree at images 5–6 and final colophon at 679; linked Google Books landing page was accessible.
sources.limitations: Original pages not inspected. Keep distinct from the Mozarabic Missale mixtum despite similar titles. A 1551 witness does not itself establish a substantive revision.

catalogue_proposals.scope_limit: Fragmentary surviving copy. Establish exact title/colophon and missing extent before comparing earlier/later books.

catalogue_proposals.title: Missale Salmanticense
catalogue_proposals.scope_limit: Inspect title, episcopal front matter, colophon and predecessor witnesses; a new printing is not sufficient evidence of reform.

catalogue_proposals.holding: Biblioteca Universitaria de Sevilla, A Res. 10/1/06
catalogue_proposals.scope_limit: Inspect original front matter and colophon, then identify earlier local books and later reception. No revision or effective date inferred.

catalogue_proposals.holding: Bibliothèque municipale de Lyon, SJ L 013/14
catalogue_proposals.scope_limit: Catalogue explicitly identifies Roman use. Inspect title and authority front matter; compare older/later Toledo Roman books independently of the Hispanic tradition.

Usuarium's 11 December 2025 report describes 283 processed Mass books from 247 institutions; this is a dated project report, not a count of distinct recensions or evidence that this repository's 151 trajectories are exhaustive.

eastern_church_coverage.label: Albanian Greek Catholic tradition

dossier_coverage.scope: No book state is documented. A gap-only tradition in eastern-local-round2 names the missing celebrant book and records the searches made; prior inventory witnesses or relationships remain usable.
dossier_coverage.reception_limit: Mapped stages concern identified source books or relevant recensions. This crosswalk does not create a local adoption or continuous-use claim.
dossier_coverage.date_limit: Stage dates are the canonical dossier values, not an uninterrupted period of use or local adoption. Complementary-volume completion dates remain distinct from first-volume publication.

eastern_church_coverage.missing_stage_chain: No exact Elbasan Catholic celebrant book is established. Inspect mission inventories and original reports for title, imprint, approval, received exemplar and dated use; resolve current census classification separately. Orthodox Albanian and Italo-Albanian books remain unassigned to this row. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): OPAC SBN BVE0501507 identifies a 55-page Albanian–Italian Chrysostom booklet ([1979?]) whose title names the Catholic-Byzantine church of St Peter, Elbasan; its title leaf, issuer, role, approval and any dated use are uninspected, and its date falls in the 1967–1990 worship ban. The Dicastery's 2017 and 2019 reference works place the Apostolic Administration of Southern Albania among Eastern Catholics without their own hierarchy; a current named census remains unobtained. Batch 5 (2026-10-22): the gap is now the named dossier row eastern-local-round2:albanian-book. New bounded searches found no book: OPAC SBN any-field queries (Papamihali, Scarpelli Pietro, mesha hyjnore, Gojarti, Gojarit, Joan Gojarti liturgjia, shqiperia bizantine liturgjia and Elbasan, all 21 Elbasan records screened) return BVE0501507 as the only liturgical record; Internet Archive metadata found no Albanian Catholic service book; the National Library of Albania catalogue API returned unusable responses instead of search results. Census framing: the latest official named enumeration found is Cardinal Sandri's list of 15 November 2016, which names an Albanian Church; no later official named list was reachable.

next_sources.inspection: DGA 2007 census printed pp. 244, 374 and 496 checked against page images; Jemi article references and Gori 2021 archive description read. The mission originals and liturgical books themselves remain uninspected.
next_sources.target: ACCO Prot. 441/28, especially Scarpelli’s 10 January 1930 report, Nr. X, pp. 37–50; de Meester–Scarpelli correspondence at the Greek College; an Elbasan Catholic book inventory and exact title/approval/use leaves. Current owning route limit: No exact Elbasan Catholic celebrant book is established. Inspect mission inventories and original reports for title, imprint, approval, received exemplar and dated use; resolve current census classification separately. Orthodox Albanian and Italo-Albanian books remain unassigned to this row. Batch 4 (2026-10-21): inspect the Grottaferrata state-library copy of OPAC SBN BVE0501507 (Albanian–Italian Chrysostom naming the Elbasan Catholic-Byzantine church, [1979?]) and chapter 35 of The Catholic East (2019); obtain a current named Annuario or Dicastery enumeration. byzantine.rule: Audit Chrysostom, Basil and Presanctified separately. Liturgikon does not alone establish complete lections, variable hymns or calendar; identify Apostolos, Gospel, Typikon and other complementary books as applicable. Rubrical Ordo and private/solemn celebration provisions need their own scope.

alexandrian.rule: Identify which anaphoras and language layers each witness contains. Coptic and Ge’ez are separate. Establish separate lection/chant sources and local calendrical reception; notation added to a new book does not date all chant texts.

armenian.rule: Identify celebrant and minister/choir books and complementary volumes. Do not turn Latin translations or two 1677 components into successive Armenian-rite whole missals. Keep the existing Google-controlled 1677 Lyturgia/Ministerium and the distinct FSL A/711 EAP 19-page setting separate; native wording, book completeness, reception and ancestry require their own evidence.

syriac.rule: Track common order and anaphora selection separately; identify Syriac, Garshuni and Arabic roles. A shared ancient anaphora does not prove identical later Catholic books or common approval.

east-syriac.rule: Keep ordinary/anaphoras, propers, epistle and gospel books distinct. Source reform and local implementation can have different dates. Chaldean and Syro-Malabar revision chains must not be collapsed.

western.rule: Map content actually represented: sacramentary, missal, ordinal, lectionary and gradual need not contain the same components. A pericope or preparation-prayer relationship cannot establish whole-missal ancestry. Calendar supplements are bounded components. Complete bounded offertory and strict Canon constituents remain partial whole-Missal text coverage; a full-constituent comparison does not establish complete-book ancestry. The 1606 post-Canon and 1657 two-form Pater are independently bounded constituents, while both whole Missals stay partial. The wider 1657 continuation remains blocked by explicit source damage; comparison and native parent declarations remain distinct.

unassigned-eucharistic.rule: Inventory holding bucket only. Blank source country/origin/genre labels do not identify a rite, Church or local use. Establish book identity, ceremonial role, contents, language, authority and reception from original sources before assigning a canonical tradition.

component_findings.finding: The study compares the 1950 priestly prayer book and 1953 Sluzhebnik calendars: the former supplies troparia/kontakia absent from the latter. This is a complementary-book allocation question, not evidence that the rite lost those texts.
component_findings.consequence: A Liturgikon-only chronology cannot certify complete propers; reception still requires local evidence.

component_findings.finding: The Liturgikon contains celebrant material for several services but relies on other liturgical books. Identify lectionary, chant and calendar dependencies separately.
component_findings.consequence: Do not equate a three-Liturgy volume with the full source corpus for every celebration.

inventory_followup.finding: SICO 2009, printed p. 291, records recognitio on 2009-12-09 for Macedonian Chrysostom and Basil; the online register calls the same dated action approval. The same bytes were re-acquired on 2026-10-20 and the SICO page image rechecked. A newly inspected official pastoral letter requests thanksgiving liturgies on 3 December 2023 without naming a book or its language. Vatican News authenticates the identity and September 2024 presentation of a jubilee monograph by Goce Kostov and Zoran I. Stojanov. An unauthenticated third-party extract apparently from that monograph supplies a concrete Литургикон (2009) title lead and five companion-title leads; the original monograph pages and every service-book title leaf remain unverified. The six titles cannot all be assigned to the Byzantine route because Stojanov also governs the Latin diocese. No exact source-language edition, contents census, actual use of the approved wording, independent textual stage, or transmission edge is established.

focused_gap_dispositions.finding: Glevaňák p.119 describes Prešov and Mukachevo using the Lviv 1905 Liturgikon. Pages 117–121 describe review of the Roman books, Gojdič’s 13 June 1943 implementation letter, interruption in 1950, Hopko’s 1966 appeal, and continued Galician-book practice. This supports historical shared-book reception and uneven reform implementation, not a unique Slovak edition or universal 1942 replacement.
focused_gap_dispositions.required_evidence: Inspect cited archive originals and exact local copies. Confirm each proposed implementation date and component before creating reception transitions.

inventory_followup.finding: Glevaňák (2006), p. 119, reports Prešov and Mukachevo use of the 1905 Lviv Liturgikon. This supports reception of a shared book, not a distinct Slovak edition. His account of interrupted Roman-book implementation does not establish universal adoption. SICO reports Slovak Chrysostom approval on 1997-09-14, Prot. N. 45/78. The official register reports Slovak Basil and Presanctified approval on 2004-05-29. Boháč attributes the later translations to the 1940 Grottaferrata Chrysostom and 1952 Rome Liturgikon and reports local Chrysostom introduction on 1998-02-22. Approval, source selection, publication and local use remain distinct facts.

focused_gap_dispositions.finding: The Vulgata study names Russian, Bulgarian and Serbian intended users. The official Burgas listing identifies a 2005 composite service/prayer book; it does not establish a source-language altar edition. Neither fact demonstrates Bulgarian adoption of a particular Roman Vulgata printing.
focused_gap_dispositions.required_evidence: Bulgarian copy or local implementation record for Vulgata; 2005 title, contents, language and source/approval statement.

focused_gap_dispositions.finding: Bogataj identifies the 1942 Ruthenian Church Slavonic book as the source for the approved Slovenian translation in Križevci and says the Slavonic text continues alongside it. focused_gap_dispositions.required_evidence: Original letters and exact 1942 copy; earlier and other jurisdictional inventories.
